title: Jassa Singh Rejoins the Khalsa and Ram Rauni Becomes Ramgarh

blocks.text: This page completes the reconciliation by describing a petition sent by arrow into the fort, allowing Jassa Singh to seek acceptance without breaking the lines. Once the message is received, the estrangement is set aside and he is welcomed back into the Khalsa with the men who came in the same spirit.

The page then widens from personal reunion to political change. Mir Mannu recalls his forces toward the crisis elsewhere, while Kaura Mal secures Sikh help by negotiation, gifts, and recognition that the Khalsa must be treated as a real power rather than a hunted remnant.

In that changed setting Ram Rauni acquires new stature and begins to be remembered as Ramgarh. What began as a desperate enclosure around Amritsar is recast as a fortified Sikh center linked to alliance, revenue, and restored unity.
